title: Count the Number of Fair Pairs
summary: Given an array of integers and a range defined by lower and upper bounds, count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j, and the sum of the elements at these indices falls within the given range.
statement: Given an array of integers and a range defined by lower and upper bounds, count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j, and the sum of the elements at these indices falls within the given range.
constraints: A pair is fair when lower <= nums[i]+nums[j] <= upper.
Return the number of fair pairs.
hints: Sort the values so valid partners for one value form a contiguous interval.
For each index, binary-search the first partner reaching lower-value.
Binary-search just after the last partner at most upper-value, restricting both searches to later indices.
The difference of those bounds counts every fair pair once at its smaller index.
editorial: The difference of those bounds counts every fair pair once at its smaller index.

tests.explanation: Six index pairs have sums between three and six inclusive.
Only values two and nine sum to exactly eleven.
